- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days), suggesting a persistent upward bias.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, indicating an overshoot after spikes, followed by premature mean reversion.
- In low-price regimes (e.g., 2023-11-28/29), model forecasts remain stubbornly high while true prices fall sharply, suggesting failure to capture downward momentum or volatility.
- Model exhibits strong lag in adjusting to true price drops — often underestimates the depth of corrections.
- Forecasts show little sensitivity to recent price declines; model inertia persists even when true prices are falling rapidly.
- In high-price regimes (e.g., 2022-11-28/29), model overreacts to short-term spikes, leading to overestimation of subsequent price levels.
- Model fails to account for mean reversion in the short term — often forecasts remain elevated longer than actual price corrections.
- Forecasts are overly smooth, lacking volatility spikes that align with true price behavior, especially during sharp corrections.
- Model tends to ignore recent low-price data, leading to persistent overestimation in periods of falling prices.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 5–15% in early periods when true prices are falling, and downward by 10–20% in late periods when prices are correcting sharply.
